ln-northlander.environment: Ice-plains, glacier-fed fjords, and long white winters
ln-northlander.culture: Northlanders measure a life by the winters survived and the oaths kept through them. Every fjord-hold keeps a Saga-Stone where the year's dead and deeds are carved before the ice takes the names.
ln-northlander.tradition: The Aurora-Vigil, where the young sit a night beneath the northern lights to be judged worthy by the ancestor-fire.
ln-northlander.appearance: Weather-hardened, pale, amber and bone ornaments, storm-braided hair.
ln-northlander.naming: A given name plus an earned deed-name (Yrsa Ice-Walker).
ln-northlander.landmark: The Aurora Vault of Fjordheim, where dead kings lie under ice
hooks: A dead king is thawing out of the Aurora Vault your hold guards
You are the first of your hold to sail south instead of raiding
Your family's name was struck from the Saga-Stone and you mean to earn it back

ln-coastborn.homeland: The trade-towns of the Crownlands coast and Port Meridian
ln-coastborn.environment: Warm harbors, tide-flats, and busy sea-lanes
ln-coastborn.culture: Coastborn humans live by the tide-tables and the harbor-bell, a mercantile, cosmopolitan people who trust a signed contract more than any crown. Half of any Coastborn town is other Kin, and they like it that way.
ln-coastborn.tradition: The Launching, a coming-of-age where the young must sail a small boat out of sight of land and return.
ln-coastborn.appearance: Sun-weathered, practical sea-cloth, guild-tokens and knot-charms.
ln-coastborn.naming: Given name plus a harbor or ship-name (Del of Saltmarket).
ln-coastborn.landmark: Port Meridian, the free harbor open to every flag
hooks: A covenant blockade is strangling your home harbor
You inherited a ship with a debt and a secret hold
A century-sunk wreck has surfaced on the Graveyard Reef and your family owned it

ln-highlander.homeland: The fortress-cities of the Crownspine ridgelines
ln-highlander.environment: High mountain passes, cloud-line ridges, ancient suspension bridges
ln-highlander.culture: Highlanders of the Crownspine build fortress-cities into the mountainsides and measure adulthood by the Crossing of Nine Bridges, a pilgrimage above the cloud line. Every household keeps a Storm Bell, said to be forged from the armor of the first warrior to survive the Skyfall.
ln-highlander.tradition: The Crossing of Nine Bridges, a deadly rite across ancient chain-spans above the clouds.
ln-highlander.appearance: Wind-burned, wrapped in clan-plaid, iron bridge-tokens for each crossing.
ln-highlander.naming: Given name plus a clan-and-peak name (Maerin of Bridgehold).
ln-highlander.landmark: The Nine Bridges of Ninebridge Hold
hooks: A bridge is failing and the Warden hides it to save face
Your household's Storm Bell cracked, an ill omen you must answer
You refused the Crossing and are called coward until you make it

ln-desertborn.homeland: The oasis-cities and caravan-roads of the Sunscorch
ln-desertborn.environment: Dune-seas, killing daytime heat, cold star-bright nights
ln-desertborn.culture: Desertborn live by water-law and the caravan-road, a people for whom hospitality is survival and a shared canteen is a sacred bond. They read the dunes for the buried cities that the sand keeps and the sand-readers forbid.
ln-desertborn.tradition: The Water-Oath, where sharing your last water with a stranger binds you both as kin for life.
ln-desertborn.appearance: Dust-veiled, layered sun-robes, sun-gold jewelry, sand-scoured skin.
ln-desertborn.naming: Given name plus an oasis or caravan-name (Sael of Karan).
hooks: A sandstorm uncovered a city that should have stayed buried
You carry a map the sand-readers would kill to keep hidden
Your caravan's water-oath partner betrayed the road

ln-cityborn.homeland: The great walled market-cities like Highreach
ln-cityborn.environment: Crowded guild-quarters, walled streets, imperial ruins beneath the cellars
ln-cityborn.culture: Cityborn are the guild-and-charter humans of the Crownlands' free cities, raised among a dozen Kin in one street. Ambition here is measured in charters won and ledgers balanced, and everyone is three favors from the Goldhand League.
ln-cityborn.tradition: The Charter-Day, when a young citizen is entered into a guild's rolls and gains a name in the city's records.
ln-cityborn.appearance: Well-dressed by trade and station, guild-badges, city-fashion.
ln-cityborn.naming: Given name plus a guild or district (Corin of the Lantern Ward).
ln-cityborn.landmark: The Sundered Throne kept under glass in Highreach's imperial hall
hooks: The Sundered Throne in your city whispered a name last winter
Your guild charter is being stolen out from under you
An imperial vault opened beneath your district and something came up

ln-wildborn-h.homeland: The frontier forest-towns like Green Hollow
ln-wildborn-h.environment: The tree line where farmland meets old-growth Wilds
ln-wildborn-h.culture: Wildborn humans are frontier folk who live where the Emerald Wilds press against settled land, half-farmer and half-ranger. They keep the old woodland courtesies to avoid waking what sleeps under the canopy, and they know the Hunt by its horn.
ln-wildborn-h.tradition: The Tree-Line Truce, small daily offerings left at the forest edge to keep peace with the Wilds' peoples.
ln-wildborn-h.appearance: Practical woodcraft leathers, green dyes, charms of bone and bark.
ln-wildborn-h.naming: Given name plus a homestead or wood-name (Bram of Thornwatch).
ln-wildborn-h.landmark: The tree line at Green Hollow where farm meets old growth
hooks: The Hunt rode past your town by daylight for the first time
A wolfkin range has gone silent and the settlers are blamed
You crossed the tree-line truce and owe the forest a debt

ln-stormtouched.homeland: The ridge-holds of the Stormreach storm-belt
ln-stormtouched.environment: Permanent storm-belt of chained thunderheads and standing lightning
ln-stormtouched.culture: Stormtouched humans were born under the living Storm and marked by it, their hair and eyes lit faintly with static. They court the lightning rather than hide from it, and the Stormwardens watch them closely for signs the Storm has claimed one as its own.
ln-stormtouched.tradition: The Reading of the Sky, where every Stormtouched child is taught to name a storm's mood before they can name the days.
ln-stormtouched.appearance: Static-lit hair, storm-grey eyes, faint lightning-scars, storm-glass ornaments.
ln-stormtouched.naming: Given name plus a storm-omen (Ilsa Thunder-Marked).
ln-stormtouched.landmark: The Standing Bolt, frozen lightning above Thundergate
hooks: The Storm spoke a name and it is yours
The Standing Bolt flickered the day you were born
The Stormwardens want you tested to see what the Storm made you

ln-highelf.homeland: The high-realm courts near grown-city Elarethil
ln-highelf.environment: Ancient canopy cities and luminous grown-wood spires
ln-highelf.culture: High Elves keep the oldest unbroken courts in the world, where a slight from three centuries past is still on the docket. They regard themselves as the keepers of the First Age's memory and rarely let anyone forget the debt.
ln-highelf.tradition: The Century Rite, a coming-of-age withheld until a full hundred years, when memory-weavings of the whole life are sung.
ln-highelf.appearance: Tall, poised, living-wood circlets, robes of leaf-weave and silver.
ln-highelf.naming: A long house-name and a personal name in Old Elvish (Aeltheri of House Vaelor).
ln-highelf.landmark: The Heartwood, said to remember the whole forest
hooks: You were exiled for refusing an oath your house swore before your birth
A grudge-name three centuries old is now yours to end or honor
The Heartwood is sickening and your court is blamed

ln-woodelf.homeland: The green-hollow ranges of the deep Wilds
ln-woodelf.environment: Old-growth forest, mist-groves, and living hunting-trails
ln-woodelf.culture: Wood Elves live in the forest rather than above it, keeping nature-faith and grove-law over court and crown. They share the canopy with beast-kin ranges, and cutting the wrong tree can start a war that the Greenwardens must judge.
ln-woodelf.tradition: The Grove-Naming, where a young wood elf is given into the keeping of a particular grove-spirit for life.
ln-woodelf.appearance: Lithe, bark-toned skin-marks, living-wood bows, leaf-cloaks.
ln-woodelf.naming: Given name tied to a grove or season (Faenor Springthorn).
ln-woodelf.landmark: The Silent Glade where sound will not travel
hooks: Your grove-spirit has fallen silent and you must learn why
A grove-treaty is broken and both sides want you as witness
The Hunt has begun riding by day through your range

ln-drow.homeland: The drow house-city Glimmerreach in the Blackdeep
ln-drow.environment: Lightless caverns lit by glowfall and deep-crystal
ln-drow.culture: The Drow descended into the Blackdeep in an exile no surface elf will fully explain, and there built house-cities ruled by matriarchs and endless succession-wars. Not all are cruel, but all are careful, for in the dark a lantern is a target.
ln-drow.tradition: The Silence-Rite, where a young drow proves they can move, hunt, and kill without a sound.
ln-drow.appearance: Ashen or dusk-dark skin, white and silver hair, blind-pearl eyes, shadow-silk.
ln-drow.naming: House-name and personal name, often with a shadow-epithet (Xel'ryn of House Mornvael).
ln-drow.landmark: The Glowfall, an underground waterfall of luminous stone
hooks: A house-matron summons you home for a war you fled
The Glowfall is going dark tunnel by tunnel
You were made expendable precisely so a house could trust you

ln-elarin.homeland: The silver villages of the Moonlit Vale's edge
ln-elarin.environment: Perpetual dusk, moon-silvered mist, and turning woods
ln-elarin.culture: The Elarin are the twilight elves of the Vale's border, neither fully of the moon-courts nor the Wilds, keepers of threshold-lore and the paths between places. They are famed guides for those who must cross where the Vale bleeds into the Shadowlands.
ln-elarin.tradition: The Threshold-Walk, a rite of crossing the Turning Wood alone and returning by a different path than one left.
ln-elarin.appearance: Dusk-pale, silver-eyed, grey and violet weaves, threshold-charms.
ln-elarin.naming: Given name plus a path or threshold (Ilyra Duskgate).
ln-elarin.landmark: The Turning Wood where paths rearrange by moonlight
hooks: A path in the Turning Wood now leads somewhere it never did
You must guide someone across the shadow-border who should not cross
You returned from the Threshold-Walk by a path that no longer exists

ln-moonelf.culture: Moon Elves live by lunar tides and dream-omens in the courts of the Vale, reading fate in the fate-showing waters of Silvermere. Their politics are fought with secrets and omens, and a shared dream can seal an alliance or start a feud.
ln-moonelf.tradition: The Fate-Gazing, when a young moon elf first looks into Silvermere and is told, or refuses to be told, their fate.
ln-moonelf.appearance: Luminous pale skin, moon-silver hair, dream-silk robes, lunar tattoos.
ln-moonelf.naming: Given name plus a lunar phase (Seluné Waning-Star).
ln-moonelf.landmark: Silvermere, the lake that shows not your face but your fate
hooks: Silvermere showed you a fate you refuse to accept
A dream-thief is stealing memories from your court
Three strangers were shown the same fate and one is you

ln-sunelf.homeland: The sun-caravans and oasis-courts of the Sunscorch
ln-sunelf.environment: Golden dune-seas and oasis gardens under a killing sun
ln-sunelf.culture: Sun Elves are the desert-caravan elves who traded the shaded courts for the open sun, keepers of star-charts and oasis-law along the Sunscorch roads. Where other elves hoard memory, sun elves trade it, selling old maps and older secrets.
ln-sunelf.tradition: The Star-Reckoning, where a young sun elf must navigate the deep dunes by star-chart alone.
ln-sunelf.appearance: Bronze-gold skin, sun-white hair, desert weaves and sun-gold ornaments.
ln-sunelf.naming: Given name plus a star or oasis (Aurelin of the Twin Stars).
ln-sunelf.landmark: Sunspire, the mile-high needle that casts no shadow at noon
hooks: Your caravan's star-chart leads to a city the sand-readers sealed
The Sunspire's tip has begun to glow and only you noticed
A rival is selling forged maps under your family's mark

ln-starelf.homeland: The star-courts near the Threshold of the Celestial Heights
ln-starelf.environment: Rarefied luminous heights of starlight and aurora
ln-starelf.culture: Star Elves are the rarest elven line, dwelling at the edge of the Celestial Heights among the seraphim, keepers of constellation-lore and the oldest prophecies. They are half in the world and half out of it, and time runs strangely where they live.
ln-starelf.tradition: The Constellation-Naming, where a newborn is bound to a star-pattern that guides and, some say, dooms them.
ln-starelf.appearance: Star-pale, luminous eyes, hair like captured light, star-glass ornaments.
ln-starelf.naming: Given name plus a constellation (Vaeloth of the Crown of Nine).
ln-starelf.landmark: The Star Court where the constellations hold council
hooks: Your bound constellation has begun to go dark
A prophecy in the Star Court names your character
A Fallen seraph asks you to carry word the Choir forbids

ln-durnak.culture: The Durnak are the great forge-city dwarves of Durnhal, keepers of the Everforge that has burned since before the Sundering. Their whole society is craft-and-ledger: a dwarf is known by their masterwork and the debts recorded in their beard-braids.
ln-durnak.tradition: The First Masterwork, presented before the Forgemoot to earn adult standing and a maker's-mark.
ln-durnak.appearance: Broad, soot-marked, rune-braided beards, heirloom metalwork.
ln-durnak.naming: Given name, clan-name, and maker's-mark (Thordin Ironvault, Mark of the Twin Anvils).
hooks: The Everforge is dimming and rival clans blame each other
Your first masterwork was stolen before its presentation
A forge-master vanished in the deep levels below the city

ln-mountain.homeland: The mountain-clan holds of the high Ironspine
ln-mountain.environment: Alpine peaks, mountain-halls, and mining tunnels
ln-mountain.culture: Mountain Dwarves keep the old clan-holds and mining-law of the high peaks, less refined than the forge-cities but prouder of their independence. They quarry the ore the everforges need and never let the Forgemoot forget who digs it.
ln-mountain.tradition: The Vein-Right, an inherited claim to a particular ore-vein that a dwarf must work to keep.
ln-mountain.naming: Given name plus a clan and peak (Vera Stonehelm of Greypeak).
rivals: Deep dwarves over the lower veins
ln-mountain.landmark: Cloudanvil, the anvil-shaped peak of the high clans
hooks: A vein-right dispute is about to become a clan war
Your clan's oldest mine broke into something older
The Forgemoot means to seize your family's vein

ln-deep.homeland: The under-city Lowvault in the Blackdeep
ln-deep.environment: Lightless deep tunnels, fungal forests, cavern-seas
ln-deep.culture: Deep Dwarves dwell far below the forge-cities in Lowvault, keeping the Deep Conclave's peace and the surface out. They dig deeper than any other dwarves dare, and they alone keep watch on the Deepest Door, below which even they refuse to go.
ln-deep.tradition: The Deep-Watch, a solitary vigil kept over the Deepest Door as a rite of trust.
ln-deep.naming: Given name plus a depth or vault (Brakka of the Ninth Deep).
rivals: Whatever knocks on the Deepest Door
ln-deep.landmark: The Deepest Door, below which the Deep folk refuse to dig
hooks: Something is coming up through the Deepest Door you guard
The Glowfall is going dark and the Deep is losing its light
A surface expedition wants you to guide them past the Conclave's ban

ln-forgeborn.homeland: The rune-forges of Emberdeep and Durnhal
ln-forgeborn.culture: Forgeborn are the runewright dwarves, born to families that bind magic into steel. Their masterworks are prayers in metal, and a Forgeborn is buried with their finest rune, that their craft may speak for them to the ancestors.
ln-forgeborn.tradition: The Rune-Waking, when a young Forgeborn inscribes their first living rune and it either wakes or shatters.
ln-forgeborn.appearance: Rune-scarred hands, glowing forge-marks, ember-cloth aprons.
ln-forgeborn.naming: Given name plus a rune-lineage (Kild Emberrune).
hooks: A living rune you forged has begun to change on its own
Your family's master-rune was stolen
The knocking on the Sealed Door keeps the rhythm of a rune you know

ln-stoneborn.homeland: The stonemason-holds of the Ironspine passes
ln-stoneborn.culture: Stoneborn are the builder-dwarves, masons and bridge-wrights whose stonework is meant to outlast the mountains it is cut from. They hold that the dead live on in the stone they shaped, and a Stoneborn hall is a graveyard and a monument at once.
ln-stoneborn.tradition: The Setting of the First Stone, laid by a young Stoneborn to found something meant to stand for centuries.
ln-stoneborn.naming: Given name plus a work or hold (Dwalia of the Long Bridge).
ln-stoneborn.landmark: The Long Bridge of glacier stone across a frozen fjord
hooks: A bridge your ancestors built is failing and only your family's stone-lore can save it
A tomb you set is being robbed
Your first stone was laid on cursed ground

ln-runebeard.homeland: The runebeard enclaves within the forge-cities
ln-runebeard.culture: Runebeards are the loremaster-dwarves who keep the grudge-archives and favor-archives, their beards braided with rune-rings that record every debt and deed of their line. They are the memory and the conscience of the forge-cities, feared for what they remember.
ln-runebeard.tradition: The Braiding of the First Ring, when a young Runebeard is entrusted with their line's ledger of debts.
ln-runebeard.appearance: Elaborate rune-ringed beards, ink-stained fingers, archive-keys.
ln-runebeard.naming: Given name plus a ledger-line (Balgrim of the Iron Ledger).
rivals: Those who would erase a recorded debt
hooks: A grudge in your ledger names someone you love
Someone is trying to erase a debt from the archive
The Grudge That Ended a Kingdom has come due in your generation

ln-hearthborn.homeland: The settled shires of the green Crownlands
ln-hearthborn.environment: Rolling farm-shires, round-doored hill-homes, hedgerow lanes
ln-hearthborn.culture: Hearthborn halflings keep the settled shires where a good reputation and a fuller table matter more than any law. A shire runs on the Long Table, shared meals where grievances are spoken once and then dropped forever.
ln-hearthborn.tradition: The Long Table, a communal feast where every quarrel must be aired and then buried under the next course.
ln-hearthborn.appearance: Comfortable, waistcoated, apple-cheeked, luck-charms on watch-chains.
ln-hearthborn.naming: Given name plus a family and shire (Poppy Underhill of Greenmeadow).
ln-hearthborn.landmark: The great Long Tables of the shire-moots
hooks: Your shire sits atop an imperial vault a duke means to seize
A recipe your family guards is worth killing for
You are the first Hearthborn in memory to leave the shire for good

ln-riverfoot.homeland: The barge-roads and river-ports of the Crownlands
ln-riverfoot.environment: Slow rivers, stilt-towns, and busy barge-lanes
ln-riverfoot.culture: Riverfoot halflings live on the water, a barge-folk of traders and pilots who know every current and every fence between the mountains and the sea. Their homes float, their loyalties run deep, and their gossip travels faster than the tide.
ln-riverfoot.tradition: First-Foot, the belief that whoever first crosses a barge's deck at new year shapes its luck.
ln-riverfoot.appearance: Bright waistcoats, river-tan, knot-charms, pole-callused hands.
ln-riverfoot.naming: Given name plus a barge or river (Milo Quickcurrent).
hooks: Your barge was chosen to smuggle something you were not told about
A diver in Bridgewater came up speaking a dead tongue
The river-guild wants your family's oldest route

ln-hillborn.homeland: The hill-clan holds of the Crownlands uplands
ln-hillborn.culture: Hillborn halflings keep the old hill-clans and the standing-stone rites, a hardier, more clannish folk than their shire cousins. They herd the downs, mind the old stones, and remember the songs of who lies beneath them.
ln-hillborn.tradition: The Standing-Stone Vigil, a night spent among the old stones to be welcomed into the clan.
ln-hillborn.appearance: Weather-brown, homespun and wool, stone-charms and sling-cords.
ln-hillborn.naming: Given name plus a hill-clan (Rowan of the Grey Downs).
rivals: Those who disturb the old stones
ln-hillborn.landmark: The old standing stones of the Grey Downs
hooks: Something has been disturbed among your clan's standing stones
A stone-vigil showed you a song about the buried dead
Raiders are driving your clan off the downs

ln-meadowborn.homeland: The meadow-villages at the edge of the Emerald Wilds
ln-meadowborn.environment: Wildflower meadows where forest meets farmland
ln-meadowborn.culture: Meadowborn halflings live in the flower-country at the Wilds' edge, keepers of bee-lore, herb-craft, and the small courtesies that keep the forest peoples friendly. They are the Wilds' most trusted human-sized neighbors, and their honey seals more treaties than swords.
ln-meadowborn.tradition: The Blooming, a spring rite where the young plant a meadow whose flowers will bloom the year they come of age.
ln-meadowborn.naming: Given name plus a flower or meadow (Clover Honeyfield).
ln-meadowborn.landmark: The wildflower meadows of the Wilds' edge
hooks: A blight is spreading from the forest into your meadows
Your family's honey is the only cure for a spreading sickness
The Wilds have called in a debt your village owes

ln-wanderfoot.environment: The open road, in rambling caravan-wagons
ln-wanderfoot.culture: Wanderfoot halflings never settled, a caravan-folk of tinkers, traders, and story-keepers who follow the road-elders from town to town. They carry news, mend what is broken, and know the roads better than any map, and they never sleep twice in one place if they can help it.
ln-wanderfoot.tradition: The Luck-Token, passed to a young Wanderfoot on their first road, said to hold the luck of every mile the family has walked.
ln-wanderfoot.appearance: Layered travelling-cloth, road-dust, jingling charm-belts, patched wagons.
ln-wanderfoot.naming: Given name plus a road-name (Fen of the Long Way).
ln-wanderfoot.landmark: The great trade-crossroads of the Crownlands
hooks: You lost the caravan road home and must find it again
A luck-token you carry is wanted by someone who kills for it
The road-elder entrusted you with a debt older than the caravan

ln-luckborn.environment: Wherever fortune is courted and feared
ln-luckborn.culture: Luckborn halflings are those said to be touched by living luck, born on a lucky hour and marked by uncanny fortune. Other halflings both prize and fear them, for a Luckborn's good luck has a way of spending someone else's, and the Luckless Wanderer's tale is a warning they all know.
ln-luckborn.tradition: The Reckoning of Luck, where a Luckborn learns to give away fortune before it turns and takes from those they love.
ln-luckborn.appearance: Ordinary but for uncanny near-misses; four-leaf and coin charms worn openly.
ln-luckborn.naming: Given name plus a luck-omen (Tansy Ninelives).
ln-luckborn.landmark: The shrine of the Luckless Wanderer
hooks: Your luck has begun to fail and you must learn why
Someone believes your luck was stolen from them
You carry a luck-token said to have saved nine lives

ln-ironblood.homeland: The iron-clan holds of the Ironspine
ln-ironblood.environment: Mountain forges and iron-mines shared with the dwarves
ln-ironblood.culture: Ironblood orcs are the mountain-clans who share the Ironspine with the dwarves, master smiths and shield-bearers whose oaths are literally forged into their armor. An Ironblood's oath-scars and armor-runes are read as a resume of every promise they have kept.
ln-ironblood.tradition: Oath-scars, ritual marks made when a binding promise is sworn, and armor-runes forged to record it.
ln-ironblood.naming: Given name and a deed-name earned young (Grukka Shield-Sworn).
ln-ironblood.landmark: The shared forge-holds of the Ironspine
hooks: An oath forged into your armor now binds you to a cause you doubt
Your clan owes a blood-oath only you can fulfill
A rival clan claims your oath-scars are false

ln-ashborn.environment: Grey volcanic desert, ashfall, and ember-storms
ln-ashborn.culture: Ashborn orcs are the ash-clans of the burned south, who live off what the fire left and hold the Everburn half-sacred. Their scholars keep the true history of the Age of Ash and bristle at the lie that every orc is only a warrior.
ln-ashborn.tradition: The Ash-Vigil, a night spent alone in the burned lands to hear the ancestors in the ember-wind.
ln-ashborn.appearance: Ash-grey skin, ember-red eyes, salt-cured leathers, ash-marks.
ln-ashborn.naming: Given name and an ash-deed (Vorag Ember-Walker).
ln-ashborn.landmark: The Glass Capital, fused to obsidian in a single night
hooks: The Everburn is spreading toward your stronghold
An ash-vigil showed you a name that should be dead
A vault in the Glass Capital never burned and everyone wants it

ln-frostborn-o.environment: Arctic ice-plains, glacier-halls, and frozen fjords
ln-frostborn-o.culture: Frostborn orcs are the frost-clans of the north, one people with the ash-clans until the catastrophe scattered them. They keep longbarrows and ice-halls, smoke and freeze their winters' meat, and hold that the cold itself judges the worthy.
ln-frostborn-o.tradition: The Earning of the Name in the deep winter, when a young orc's given name is replaced by a deed done in the cold.
ln-frostborn-o.appearance: Frost-white skin, pale eyes, heavy furs, iron oath-marks.
ln-frostborn-o.naming: Given name and a cold-deed (Skarn Frost-Sworn).
ln-frostborn-o.landmark: The Frozen Fleet locked in a harbor of ice
hooks: The Winter Hunt has crossed into your clan's range
A frost-clan and ash-clan reunion could heal or reopen an ancient split
The Frozen Fleet's ice is cracking and something rides in it

ln-wildborn-o.homeland: The free ranges at the Wilds' frontier
ln-wildborn-o.environment: Forest-edge frontier, open plains, and beast-kin ranges
ln-wildborn-o.culture: Wildborn orcs are the free-range clans who refuse both the mountain forges and the fixed holds, roaming the frontier and living by the older, wilder oaths. They ride, hunt, and raid by a code that the settled clans find crude and the settled clans cannot match in open country.
ln-wildborn-o.tradition: The Free-Oath, sworn to the land itself rather than to any hold, and never to be fenced.
ln-wildborn-o.appearance: Lean, sun-marked, hide and bone, wind-worn oath-marks.
ln-wildborn-o.naming: Given name and a range-deed (Ureth Plains-Runner).
ln-wildborn-o.landmark: The open frontier ranges of the Wilds' edge
hooks: Settlers are fencing the range your free-oath is sworn to
Your clan's old raiding-debt has come back to find you
The Hunt now rides the same range as your clan

ln-warborn.homeland: The war-clan holds of the Marches border
ln-warborn.environment: The contested elemental frontier and old battlefields
ln-warborn.culture: Warborn orcs are the border war-clans, oath-band infantry sworn to hold the Elemental Marches against what spills from the rifts. They are the steadiest soldiers in the world, fighting as one because breaking formation breaks an oath, and they hire out as the most disciplined mercenaries alive.
ln-warborn.tradition: The Band-Oath, sworn between an entire war-band so that each fights for the others unto death.
ln-warborn.appearance: Scarred, disciplined, matched war-plate, band-marks shared across the unit.
ln-warborn.naming: Given name and a battle-deed (Morg Gate-Holder).
ln-warborn.landmark: The Tempered Gate, forged to hold an elemental tide
hooks: The Standing Rift is widening and your band is oath-bound to hold it
Your war-band's oath was broken and you alone survived to answer for it
A mercenary contract turns out to serve a rift-cult

ln-bloodmoon.homeland: The shadow-border clans near the Vale
ln-bloodmoon.environment: Twilight border-country where the light thins
ln-bloodmoon.culture: Bloodmoon orcs are the shadow-touched clans of the border, marked by the red moon under which they keep their oaths. Feared by other orcs for the darker rites they inherited from the Blood Wars, they hold the shadow-border that no settled clan will keep.
ln-bloodmoon.tradition: The Bloodmoon Oath, sworn only under the red moon and never spoken of by daylight.
ln-bloodmoon.appearance: Dusk-dark skin, red-moon eyes, shadow-marked oath-scars, dark iron.
ln-bloodmoon.naming: Given name and a moon-deed (Kravok Redmoon-Sworn).
rivals: Clans who fear the bloodmoon rites
hooks: A bloodmoon oath binds you to a cause you no longer believe
The Unlit are recruiting from your border-clan
Other orcs have named your clan for a Blood Wars crime you did not commit

ln-drakari.environment: The permanent storm-belt of chained thunderheads
ln-drakari.culture: The Drakari are the storm-scaled dragonborn of the Stormreach, born under the living Storm and taught to read its moods before they can name the days. Their whole culture courts the lightning, raising ridge-halls to catch it, and the Stormwardens draw their oracles from Drakari lines.
ln-drakari.tradition: The First Breath, when a young Drakari's storm-breath first wakes, timed if possible to a passing tempest.
ln-drakari.appearance: Storm-violet scales, static-lit crests, storm-glass ornaments.
ln-drakari.naming: Draconic given name and a storm-omen (Vaethyr Skyborn).
hooks: Your storm-breath woke wrong, in an element not of the storm
The Standing Bolt is dying and your line's oracles are blamed
The Storm spoke a name in your voice

ln-stormborn-d.homeland: The wandering storm-camps of the Stormreach coast
ln-stormborn-d.environment: The storm-front where tempest meets sea
ln-stormborn-d.culture: Stormborn dragonborn ride the storm-front itself, a bolder, wilder cousin to the ridge-bound Drakari, kin to the Gale Riders in spirit. They believe the Storm should be freed, not caged, and their feud with the Stormwardens is the great argument of the Stormreach.
ln-stormborn-d.tradition: The Storm-Ride, a rite of gliding the leading edge of a living tempest and returning alive.
ln-stormborn-d.naming: Draconic given name and a wind-deed (Zerath Gale-Rider).
ln-stormborn-d.landmark: The Eye, the permanent hole of calm at the storm's center
hooks: You claim to have walked into the Eye and come back changed
The Stormwardens mean to cage the Storm your kin would free
A storm-ride went wrong and left you owing the tempest

ln-wyrmblood.homeland: The old wyrm-halls of the deep Ironspine
ln-wyrmblood.culture: Wyrmblood dragonborn keep the oldest bloodlines, said to carry the truest spark of the ancient wyrms, and they hold themselves to old draconic law and long memory. Proud and hoard-minded, they guard relics of the First Age and reckon debts in centuries.
ln-wyrmblood.tradition: The Hoard-Trust, where each Wyrmblood is given one relic to guard for life and answer for to the ancestors.
ln-wyrmblood.naming: Long draconic name with an ancestral epithet (Aurdrakoth of the Elder Coil).
ln-wyrmblood.landmark: The wyrm-halls of the deep Ironspine
hooks: The relic you were trusted to guard has been stolen
An old draconic debt has come due against your line
Your hoard-trust is older and stranger than you were told

ln-emberborn.homeland: The ember-forges of the Ashen Wastes
ln-emberborn.culture: Emberborn dragonborn are the fire-scaled folk of the Ashen Wastes, master forge-smiths who work the lava-forges and walk the Everburn unburned. They tend the sacred fire alongside the ash-clans and believe their breath is a trust to temper, not to spend.
ln-emberborn.tradition: The Tempering, a rite of mastering one's own ember-breath before it masters the wielder.
ln-emberborn.appearance: Ember-red scales, heat-shimmer eyes, forge-marked, lava-glass ornaments.
ln-emberborn.naming: Draconic given name and a fire-deed (Pyrrha Embertongue).
rivals: Those who would douse the Everburn
ln-emberborn.landmark: The Everburn, the fire that has never gone out
hooks: Your ember-breath is growing beyond your Tempering
The Everburn is spreading and only a fire-tender can turn it
A pilgrim asks you to guide them into the heart of the fire

ln-frostscale.homeland: The ice-vaults of the Frostbound North
ln-frostscale.culture: Frostscale dragonborn are the cold-blooded northern line, keepers of ice-vaults and glacier-lore whose breath is the killing frost. Traced to the drowning cold of the Stormfall, they are patient and still where the ember-lines are fierce, and they guard what the ice preserves.
ln-frostscale.tradition: The Stillness, a rite of holding one's frost-breath in perfect check through a long night of cold.
ln-frostscale.appearance: Frost-white and cyan scales, frost-rimed crests, ice-glass ornaments.
ln-frostscale.naming: Draconic given name and a frost-deed (Serixis Frostcoil).
hooks: Something the ice preserved is thawing under your watch
Your frost-breath will not still and the cold is spreading
An ice-vault your line guards has been broken open

ln-tideborn-d.homeland: The tide-temples of the Sapphire coast
ln-tideborn-d.culture: Tideborn dragonborn are the water-scaled coastal line, keepers of tide-temples whose breath is the surging sea. Kin to the seaborn by long tradition, they read the tides as scripture and hold their breath a trust to the water rather than a weapon.
ln-tideborn-d.tradition: The Tide-Reading, where a young Tideborn learns to name the tide's turning before the harbor-bell.
ln-tideborn-d.appearance: Tide-blue scales, wave-marked crests, pearl-and-coral ornaments.
ln-tideborn-d.naming: Draconic given name and a tide-omen (Nerixis Tidecoil).
ln-tideborn-d.landmark: The tide-temples of the Sapphire coast
hooks: The tides are reading wrong and your temple fears the abyss
Reef-serpents are fleeing something and driving ashore near your temple
Your tide-breath answered a call from the deep
